answer: One E8 Acquisition (specifically E96 Purchase, since fully compensated by a monetary amount) with P23 transferred title from = the engineer and P22 transferred title to = the phone bidder: title runs straight from consignor to buyer. The auction house is not a party between whom title moved -- nothing in the case says it ever became legal owner of the instruments, it only handled money and controlled release of the goods. Its part is recorded via P14 carried out by (qualified with P14.1 in the role of, e.g. 'auctioneer'/'agent') on the same Purchase, plus separate E10 Transfer of Custody events for the physical/legal-custody side: engineer -> auction house (P28/P29) while it catalogued and sold the lot, and auction house -> buyer's courier for delivery. The ten-day hold on the buyer's payment and the lack of direct dealing between buyer and engineer are facts about custody, money-handling and agency, not evidence that the auction house ever held title -- CRM's own worked example for this exact configuration (Sotheby's receiving 'legal responsibility for physical custody' of a statue from its owner, to facilitate a sale) treats the auction house's role as custody only. Two separate Acquisitions would be the right model only if the auction house itself took title (e.g. a guaranteed/principal sale or a dealer buy-resell), which this case does not describe.

rejected_alternatives.option: Two E8 Acquisitions (engineer -> auction house, then auction house -> bidder)
rejected_alternatives.why_not: Would require the auction house to actually acquire legal title, which nothing in the case states -- it only held payment and controlled release of the goods. The SIG's own analogous example (thread t1376, Issue 475) models an auction house's part in a consignment sale as receiving only 'legal responsibility for physical custody' from the owner, not title; splitting title into two hops is the pattern for a dealer who genuinely buys and resells, not for an auctioneer acting as agent.

rejected_alternatives.option: P14.1 in the role of alone, with no separate custody record
rejected_alternatives.why_not: concept P14 shows P14.1 qualifies the manner of an actor's participation in the Acquisition, but the case also asserts a distinct physical/legal-custody chain (auction house held the goods, then released them to a courier) which P22/P23/P14 do not capture; that needs its own E10 Transfer of Custody event(s) via P28/P29.
